title: A shell-audit record stops refusing when the file returns, and every close door checks it
requirement: REQ-295: a shell-audit record must not refuse forever after the product file is back at its previous content, the owner of the area must be able to take a false record off with a reason, and no close path may skip the check. C01: the record keeps the file's SHA-256 and refuses only while the file matches. C02: the area owner resolves a false record with a reason; a surviving edit still refuses. C03: the acceptance is not softened and close, closeMany and task_batch all apply the check.
steps: Create a task in review and a shell-audit record for session root with the SHA-256 of the edited product file.
With the file still edited, close, closeMany and applyMany (task_batch): each refuses with product_shell_violation and the row stays review.
Put the file back at HEAD content and close: accepted, the row is done.

With a record that has no hashes (the previous format) and the file already reverted: the close refuses; the BACKEND owner resolves with a reason, the record carries resolved.by and the reason, and the close accepts.
Resolve with no reason and with the wrong area (DOCS for a plugins/ file): both refused by name.
expected: A hashed record stops refusing once the file is back at HEAD (the close accepts); a surviving product edit is refused by close, closeMany and task_batch with product_shell_violation; the BACKEND owner resolves a false record with a reason that lands in the record (resolved.by, resolved.reason) and the close then accepts; a reasonless or foreign-area resolve is refused.
failsWhen: A shell-audit record keeps refusing after the file was reverted to HEAD, a false record cannot be resolved by its area owner with a reason, a surviving product edit closes through close, closeMany or task_batch, or the resolve call accepts a reasonless/foreign-area request.
trigger: A shell command leaves a product-file edit recorded by the guard; the orchestrator tries to accept the row before and after reverting the file, and the batch tool tries the same close.
oracle: REQ-295 criteria C01 (AC-1: the record stores the SHA-256 after the command, refusal only while the file matches, return to HEAD removes it), C02 (AC-2: the area owner resolves a false record with a reason; a surviving edit still refuses) and C03 (AC-3: no close path bypasses the check), canonical brief hash a6cbca2ca783c65da3f6601d08b3490af8cf7c3819fcd05a95551a43d4b837c5; product.dsh record written by proof-guard.
realism: The recorded defect: a shell changed a product file, the guard recorded it, and after the file was reverted the row could never be closed; the false record could not be taken off; and closeMany skipped the shell gate. The scenario drives the same public service the orchestrator and the batch tool use, with the record file the guard writes.
